add: The typed body of a ReaderWrap or DelegationWrap: generation, commitment, recipient and recipient key, STAGED with its claim or LATE with its signer's AuthPin and time.
An index entry or shard-table record ending a document, or a deleted ref's documents, at a version, which masks every older version in every partition until its bucket's roll-up removes them.
A device's sealed, sorted runs of each indexed key's newest version in the partitions it holds, built as it syncs, which a search probes per candidate to apply newest wins in bounded memory.
An erasure's first push on each index ref. It rewrites the ref's erasure set and moves the head's `index_epoch`, so no index push built before it, except a CLOSURE, commits after it.
The versionless file `x` beside a ref's index roots. It lists each pending erasure's documents, as doc_key and newest erased version, and only a CUT writes it.
An index ref's head field: the version of its newest CUT. Every index push except a CLOSURE names it at its head CAS, else 409 INDEX_EPOCH.
The restore invariants: only the run's own edits, exact bytes or nothing, no stale preview, no other bytes discarded; not RS1-RS3.
A 55-minute span of a phone-indexer search pair whose close reports connect withholds to its end and fixes at a 256 KiB floor each way.

DelegationWrap: A signed wrap of RK_g to a Delegation's reader key, through which its agents read until the Delegation ends or a Suspend or non-reap revocation of one drops the key.
ReaderKey, ReaderWrap: A reader's signed X-Wing key, valid 7 days, and a KeyDelivery of RK_g to it, for reading without a leaf.
erasure, ERASE push: Destroying chosen entries' keys everywhere by a committed push on the repo's `erasure` ref naming their slots; with the search index, a CUT goes first.
git-lfs store: A repo's versionless `ur/lfs` ref of git-lfs objects, moved through the daemon with no LFS server, pruned after 30 unreferenced days (a repo setting of at least 7), and holding every object a current git tip requires.
write budget, governor: Each metadata cluster's limit of 0.8 DWPD and 50% of write IOPS for all but P0 work, whose allowances taskworker's governor publishes from measured drive bytes.
fault schedule (FS-n): A deterministic script of actor steps, barriers, store faults and clock moves, checked against FI-1 to FI-30.
fence (head): A head write raising `fence` but no version: an evacuation's or GC's also sets fence_ms, ending every earlier-arrived attempt; a refusal's records the refusal.
P0, P1, P2 (write classes): The write budget's classes: P0 (revocations, lifecycle, Removes), never queued or refused; P1 (pushes), queued per network; P2 (folds, evacuation, GC), prepaid by the P1 admissions causing it, else unfunded.
